page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the E2 server family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The CPU allocation is dedicated. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1105.98, while multi-core performance reached 1452.89. Geekbench evaluations resulted in a single-core score of 906.0 and a multi-core score of 1073.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show read-only small block cached speeds of 80.99 GB/sec, dropping to 13.03 GB/sec for large block uncached reads, and 11.11 GB/sec for large block writes.

For application-specific workloads, the server achieved 1.34 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 1.39 GB/sec. Large language model inference using a small 135M model processed prompts at 164.01 tokens per second and generated text at 64.17 tokens per second. Due to its low memory capacity and entry-level CPU performance, this instance is best suited for lightweight utility services, basic web serving, small-scale background tasks, or development environments that do not require high memory density or intensive parallel processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-2 is an entry-level, x86_64 architecture virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs and 2.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, this instance allocates a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It features no local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results place this server in the lower performance tiers, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1452.89 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1073.0. Memory bandwidth is limited, reaching 13.03 GB/sec for large block read operations. Given its constrained resource profile and low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core, the e2-highcpu-2 is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, non-resource-intensive workloads. It is best suited for basic web serving, small background tasks, Redis caching with small datasets, and simple development or testing environments.
